title: Scheduled-recovery run classification (context only, never scheduled evidence)
description: Classification block for a pass that recovers a FAILED scheduled slot into its own artifact directory, e.g. the Jul 27 2026 12:30 PM ET midday recovery (config/scheduled_tasks.json -> midday_dca_scheduled_recovery_2026_07_27). Such a pass places real orders but is NEVER scheduled evidence for the slot it recovered: it is valid only as same-day, ticker-scoped top-up context for later same-day streams. The per-stream scheduled schemas (midday_run_classification.schema.json and siblings) deliberately reject these values, and the recovery state_schema_versions are deliberately absent from run_classification.ACCEPTED_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSIONS, so no scheduled-evidence consumer can ingest one. This schema exists so a recovery-context consumer can VALIDATE such an artifact rather than having to either discard it or trust it blindly (Codex review: "Define a schema for the recovery classification"). Validating against this schema does NOT relax any trading safety rule and never promotes the artifact to scheduled evidence.

run_origin.description: Always 'scheduled_recovery'. Distinct from 'scheduled' precisely so a consumer applying the scheduled contract cannot pick this run up.

run_type.description: Recovery run type for the stream being recovered.

stream.description: Recovery stream. Always the recovered stream's name with a '_recovery' suffix, which is what near_close_dca._RECOVERY_PRIOR_CONTEXT_STREAMS matches to fold these fills into a later run's top-up guard. The intraday task fires at 11:30/13:30/14:30, so its recovery stream is slot-qualified (intraday_1430_recovery); a bare intraday_recovery is accepted for a pass that does not name its slot. The afternoon stream is absent: an afternoon recovery is the afternoon run's own repair, not prior context for it.

manual_run.description: Always false. A recovery pass is scheduled-side, not a manual override; it must not be filed under the manual-exclusion roots.

recovery_rerun.description: Always false when present. failure_recovery_policy's recovery_rerun contract covers only an in-place repair of a failure that occurred AFTER data was fetched, reusing the scheduled slot directory with run_origin='scheduled'. A separate-directory recovery pass satisfies neither condition and must not claim the flag.

trading_day.description: America/New_York trading day (YYYY-MM-DD) of both the failed slot and the recovery pass.

run_id.description: Recovery run identifier, e.g. midday_recovery_20260727_1305ET. Distinct from the scheduled slot's run_id, which was never written. minLength:1 counts whitespace, so a '   ' run_id validated here while validate_recovery_classification() rejected it via run_id.strip() -- schema-aware recovery discovery and the canonical helper disagreed about the same artifact. Narrowed to the same non-whitespace pattern latest_pointer.schema.json's recovery branch uses (codex review: 'Require a nonblank recovery run ID in the schema').

cron_id.description: Scheduler id of the scheduled task whose slot failed, e.g. a6239dae. Recorded for lineage only; it never makes this artifact evidence that the task ran.

scheduled_slot_et.description: ET wall-clock time of the scheduled slot being recovered, e.g. '12:30'.

recovery_pass_started_et.description: ET wall-clock time the recovery pass itself started, e.g. '13:05'.

state_schema_version.description: Recovery-only schema version. Deliberately NOT in run_classification.ACCEPTED_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSIONS, so a scheduled consumer rejects the artifact on version alone.

valid_scheduled_evidence.description: Always false. No completeness of the artifact set can promote a recovery pass to scheduled evidence.

valid_recovery_context.description: Always true: the artifact positively asserts recovery context, rather than merely omitting the scheduled-evidence flags. run_classification.is_top_up_context_state requires this before folding the fills into a later run's guard.

same_day_top_up_context_only.description: Always true: valid ONLY as same-day, ticker-scoped top-up context for later same-day streams.

valid_afternoon_scheduled_evidence.description: Always false when present. A recovery pass is never proof the afternoon run happened.

exclude_from_watchdog_scheduled_confirma.description: Always true when present: the watchdog must not count this artifact as confirmation that the scheduled slot ran. The pass's order IDs are still CLASSIFIED by the watchdog, via run_classification.collect_recovery_context_order_ids, so they reconcile as recovery context instead of surfacing as an unexplained broker/log discrepancy.

recovered_slot_artifact_root.description: Absolute path of the scheduled directory that was expected but never written, e.g. .../midday_dca/20260727_1230ET/.

artifact_root.description: Absolute path of this recovery pass's own artifact root, a dated sibling of the scheduled slot directory, e.g. .../midday_dca/20260727_1230ET_recovery_1305ET/.

$comment: The allOf branches BIND the identity triple: three independent enums would let a cross-stream combination such as stream='midday_recovery' with run_type='morning_dca_live_recovery' validate, which run_classification.validate_recovery_classification rejects. A schema consumer -- the very reason this file exists -- would then accept an artifact every in-repo consumer refuses (Codex review: 'Couple recovery identity fields in the schema'). The intraday slots share one contract, so they are grouped in a single branch. Keep these in sync with RECOVERY_STREAM_CONTRACTS; test_run_classification.py asserts the enums match and the correspondence tests cover the pairing.
